segments.t: The JobScheduler runs unattended background jobs while KorTTY is open. It does not require an operating system service or an active SSH terminal tab. Jobs execute automatically on a configured schedule using saved SSH connections from the Connection Manager.

On macOS and Windows, an enabled job with a future run keeps the computer from entering system sleep while korTTY is running when KTPH000Configuration KTPH002 Prevent System SleepKTPH001 is enabled, so the scheduled time remains reachable. The Scheduler uses a single wake-up for the next due run and owns no polling timer when no enabled future job exists. With no terminal connection, future or running Scheduler job, or active AI request, system sleep remains available even while the setting is checked. While a job is running, macOS does not put korTTY into App Nap. Display sleep is not blocked. Linux power inhibition is not yet supported.

Open it with KTPH000Tools KTPH002 JobScheduler...KTPH001. The dialog remembers its window position and size. The German interface now translates all labels, action names, status values, validation messages, target selectors and supporting prompts; technical protocol and format names such as SFTP, Rsync, ZIP, TAR, stdout and stderr remain unchanged.
JobScheduler supports six types of actions:
KTPH000COMMANDKTPH001 — Run a non-interactive remote shell command
KTPH000SNIPPET_SCRIPTKTPH001 — Execute a SnippetManager script on the target with optional parameters
KTPH000AI_AGENTKTPH001 — Run a headless AI agent with explicit auto-approval
KTPH000AI_SWARMKTPH001 — Broadcast one AI-agent task to all selected targets in parallel and store the combined answer as a saved swarm chat
KTPH000SFTPKTPH001 — Upload, download, sync, delete, rename, create directories, set permissions, change ownership, remote-copy, or create archives
KTPH001RSYNC_SYNCKTPH002 — Synchronize directories via external KTPH000 over SSH
The JobScheduler dialog has three tabs: KTPH000JobKTPH001, KTPH002ActionKTPH003, and KTPH004JournalKTPH005.
Use the KTPH000JobKTPH001 tab to define where and when a job runs.
Display name shown in the job list, journal, and menu-bar status.
Opens the Connection Manager selection dialog. Select individual SSH TCP servers, whole groups, or both. Mosh connections are not supported.
Optional remote directory. Use KTPH000Browse...KTPH001 to connect to the target and pick a directory when the path is not known.
KTPH000 stores bounded, redacted excerpts. KTPH001 stores full output/transcripts (KorTTY-managed secrets are still redacted).
Optional date range for the job. The job will not run outside this range.
Time window for the job (e.g., 09:00 to 17:00). Values are selected from validated time lists.
Optional repeated interval inside the active window. If set, the job runs every N minutes between window start and end.
Optional explicit start times (e.g., 09:30, 12:00, 15:30). Values are selected from validated time lists.
Optional weekday filter. Use the all-toggle to select or clear all weekdays at once.
Schedule calculations use the local system time zone. If no fixed time and no interval are configured, the next run is the window start on an allowed date.
Scheduler jobs support saved SSH TCP connections only. Mosh targets are blocked as unsupported and the reason is written to the journal.

Host-key verification is secure by default. Before unattended SSH/SFTP/Rsync execution, select the target and click KTPH000Confirm host keyKTPH001 so KorTTY stores the pinned fingerprint and OpenSSH public-key material.
The checkbox KTPH000Disable host-key verification for this jobKTPH001 disables host-key verification only for the selected job. This is unsafe and should only be used when the risk is understood.
Sudo passwords can be stored for one server or for a server group:
Server-specific sudo passwords are used first.
Group sudo passwords are used as fallback.
Stored sudo passwords are encrypted with the master password.
If the master password is locked and a job needs SSH, sudo, API, or archive secrets, the job is blocked and journaled.
For Rsync jobs, KTPH001Use sudoKTPH002 means passwordless remote sudo only through KTPH000. Stored sudo passwords are not used by the current Rsync integration.
Action Tab: Job Types and ConfigurationKTPH000
Use the KTPH000ActionKTPH001 tab to choose what the job does. The tab shows only the fields that the selected action can use, so unrelated fields are hidden. The action selector includes:

Run a SnippetManager script on the selected target. The KTPH000Snippet searchKTPH001 field filters the script dropdown by snippet name, category, language, or ID; KTPH002Snippet parametersKTPH003 passes additional arguments as one argv value per line.
Run the headless scheduler AI agent. Unattended command execution requires KTPH000Auto-approve AI commandsKTPH001 on the job.
Run the KTPH000AI SwarmKTPH001 headlessly on every selected target in parallel and combine the answers into one comparison table.
Upload a local path to a remote path.
Download a remote path to a local path.
Synchronize local and remote paths in the selected upload/download direction.
Change permissions. Numeric modes such as KTPH000 and symbolic modes such as KTPH001 are accepted.
Change owner and/or group. Owner and group buttons can query the target and show available values.
Copy a remote path to another remote path on the same target.
Synchronize one or more directories via external KTPH000 over SSH.

Path fields provide local Finder/Explorer selection where the path is local and remote directory browsing where the path is remote. Remote browsing requires a selected target and host-key verification unless the job explicitly disables host-key verification.

Snippet script jobs use the selected SnippetManager entry without requiring an open terminal tab. KorTTY resolves built-in snippet variables and stored SnippetManager variables before execution. Missing snippets, missing stored variable values, and unsupported snippet languages block the job and write the reason to the journal. Additional snippet parameters are entered one per line so values with spaces are passed as single script arguments.

AI Swarm jobs run one AI-agent prompt on KTPH000all selected targets in parallelKTPH001 over background SSH sessions — no terminal tabs are opened. Beyond the shared KTPH002AI profileKTPH003, KTPH004AI promptKTPH005, and KTPH006Auto-approve AI commandsKTPH007 fields, two swarm-specific fields apply:
How many targets run concurrently (1–16, default 4).
Restricts every agent to non-mutating commands. On by default.

Results are stored twice: the KTPH000journalKTPH001 records the run outcome, and the full conversation — including the combined per-server comparison table — is saved as a KTPH002swarm chatKTPH003 that can be reopened from the AI Manager's KTPH004Swarm ChatsKTPH005 section.

The fastest way to create an AI Swarm job is the KTPH000Schedule…KTPH001 button in the KTPH002AI Swarm tabKTPH003: it prefills a new job with the tab's current targets, prompt, AI profile, and read-only setting. See that page for recommended swarm/scheduler usage scenarios.

A scheduled swarm with KTPH000Swarm read-onlyKTPH001 off and KTPH002Auto-approve AI commandsKTPH003 on changes systems unattended. Test the prompt interactively in the AI Swarm tab before enabling such a job.

SFTP archive jobs support ZIP, password-protected ZIP, TAR, and TAR.BZ2. Archive sources and exclude patterns accept one path or pattern per line. The archive can optionally be downloaded after creation.

When KTPH005Use sudo staging for SFTP pathsKTPH006 is enabled, KorTTY stages files in a temporary location and uses sudo-assisted remote commands such as KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, and KTPH004 where elevated rights are required. Cleanup failures are written to the journal.
KTPH000 supports upload and download between the local filesystem and saved SSH TCP connections.
KTPH000UploadKTPH001: local source directories are synchronized under the remote target root.
KTPH000DownloadKTPH001: remote source directories are synchronized under the local target root.
KTPH001Delete missing filesKTPH002 adds KTPH000; it is off by default.
For downloads from multiple group targets, KorTTY writes each target into its own subdirectory below the local target root to avoid overwriting files from another server.
KorTTY builds Rsync execution as a KTPH000 argument list instead of shell-concatenating the command. The command uses KTPH001; KTPH002 is added only when the job checkbox is enabled.
KTPH000 is taken from KTPH001, unless an explicit binary path is configured in KTPH002Settings KTPH004 SFTP KTPH005 JobScheduler RsyncKTPH003.
KTPH000 must be available in KTPH001.
Host-key pinning is required unless the job explicitly disables host-key verification.
Password and private-key passphrase authentication use a temporary owner-only KTPH000 helper. Secrets, helper paths, and temporary secret-file paths are redacted before journaling.

The KTPH000JournalKTPH001 tab lists job runs with local KorTTY timestamps, status, job name, and summary. The columns KTPH002StartedKTPH003, KTPH004StatusKTPH005, KTPH006JobKTPH007, and KTPH008SummaryKTPH009 are sortable; the default order shows the newest started entries first.

The search row can match all persisted journal fields or only selected columns such as status, job, summary, stdout, stderr, and detail. Enter multiple whitespace-separated terms when every term must occur somewhere in the selected search scope; use KTPH000 inside a term as a wildcard, for example KTPH001.

Selecting a row shows stdout, stderr, and detail text. Use KTPH001Delete selectedKTPH002 to remove selected journal entries. By default, KorTTY automatically deletes scheduler journal entries older than 14 days; set the retention value to KTPH000 to keep entries indefinitely.

The protocol/detail area below the table is separated by a vertical splitter. Resize it to give the output more or less height; KorTTY stores that divider position in the global settings. In the detail text area, mark text and right-click to copy the selected text to the clipboard.

Journal statuses include successful, failed, blocked, cancelled, and running/system entries. Reasons such as locked master password, missing host-key pin, missing KTPH000/KTPH001, unsupported Mosh target, or shutdown drain are written as journal details.

When KTPH000Show Jobs status in menu barKTPH001 is enabled, KorTTY shows the scheduler status after KTPH002HelpKTPH003 only if an enabled scheduler entry exists or a job is currently running. The status shows the running job, cancellation state, or the next job with a live countdown.
Click the status menu to see:
up to five next queued jobs with start time and live countdown

Right-click the status label for a compact menu with cancel actions for running jobs and a shortcut to open JobScheduler. Cancellation requests are journaled and running SSH/Rsync work is interrupted cleanly where possible.

If KorTTY is about to exit while JobScheduler jobs are running, it shows a warning with the active job names. Choosing KTPH000CancelKTPH001 keeps KorTTY running. Choosing KTPH002Wait and quitKTPH003 starts shutdown drain mode:
new scheduled or manual job starts are blocked;
the shutdown wait is written to the journal;
KorTTY waits for running jobs to complete or cancel;
KorTTY exits automatically after the drain finishes.
Host keys are pinned by default to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks on unattended execution.
Sudo passwords are stored encrypted with the master password.
SSH key passphrases and archive passwords are stored encrypted.
KorTTY redacts managed secrets (passwords, passphrases, archive credentials) from journal output before persistence.
If the master password is locked when a job needs SSH, sudo, API, or archive secrets, the job is blocked.

KTPH002JobScheduler job is blocked:KTPH003 Open KTPH004Tools KTPH006 JobScheduler... KTPH007 JournalKTPH005 and inspect the selected entry's detail text. Common causes are:
- Locked master password
- Missing host-key pin
- Unsupported Mosh target
- Missing KTPH000 or KTPH001 in PATH
- Old host-key pin without OpenSSH public-key material for Rsync
KTPH002JobScheduler Rsync cannot start:KTPH003 Verify local KTPH000 and KTPH001, or configure the Rsync binary path in KTPH004Settings KTPH006 SFTP KTPH007 JobScheduler RsyncKTPH005.
KTPH000JobScheduler remote browser cannot open:KTPH001 Select exactly one target and confirm the host key first, unless the job explicitly disables host-key verification.
